name: Fes el Bali
description: The old walled medina, a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the world's largest car-free urban areas. A dense labyrinth of alleys, souks, tanneries, riads and historic madrasas that immerses you fully in old Fes.
bestFor: Culture seekers and short-stay travellers wanting a fully immersive medina experience

name: Fes el Jdid
tagline: Royal quarter and old Jewish Mellah
description: The smaller medieval quarter built beside the old medina, home to the royal palace gates, the historic Mellah Jewish quarter and lively markets. Quieter and more open than Fes el Bali while still deeply historic.
bestFor: Travellers wanting medina character with a slightly quieter and more navigable feel
pros: Close to both medina and new city

name: Ville Nouvelle
description: The French-built new town with wide boulevards, modern apartments, cafes, banks and coworking-friendly hotels. This is where reliable wifi, supermarkets and everyday conveniences live, offering the most comfortable long-stay base in Fes.
bestFor: Digital nomads needing reliable wifi, comfort and modern amenities long term

name: Batha
description: The transitional district around Bab Boujloud and the Batha museum, bridging the medina and Ville Nouvelle. It offers hotels, restaurants and easy medina access while staying close to modern services, making it a practical middle-ground base.
bestFor: Visitors wanting medina proximity plus quick access to modern amenities and transport
pros: Good mix of hotels and food
